West to East is - Sumatra, Java, Bali and Lombok.

Sunda Islands of Sumatra (Sumatera), Java (Jawa), the 
southern extent of Borneo (Kalimantan), and Celebes 
(Sulawesi); the Lesser Sunda Islands (Nusa Tenggara) 
of Bali and a chain of islands that runs eastward through 
Timor; the Moluccas (Maluku) between Celebes and the 
island of New Guinea; and the western extent of New 
Guinea (generally known as Papua).
• The capital, Jakarta, is located near the northwestern 
coast of Java.

Consider the following statements:
 1. On the planet Earth, the fresh water available for 
use amounts to about less than 1% of the total 
water found.
 2. Of the total freshwater found on the planet Earth, 
95% is bound up in polar ice caps and glaciers.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.question_hi:
[विश्व का भूगोल: समुद्र विज्ञान, महासागरीय धाराएँ, विश्व की नदियाँ, झीलें एवं प्रवाल भित्तियाँ • I.A.S. (Pre) 2010]
निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
Consider the following statements:
 1. On the planet Earth, the fresh water available for 
use amounts to about less than 1% of the total 
water found.
 2. Of the total freshwater found on the planet Earth, 
95% is bound up in polar ice caps and glaciers.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation_en:
96.5% of the total water available on Earth is salt water found 
in Ocean. Out of the remaining 2.5% Fresh water, 1.7% is in 
the form of glaciers and polar ice, which is unusable for us. 
So in this way total available fresh water to use is less than 
1% of the total water available on earth. Out of total amount 
of fresh water (2.5%), 68.7% is found in the form of glaciers 
and polar ice, 30.1% in the form of underground water, 0.3% 
in the form of surface water and remaining 0.9% is found in 
other forms. Hence only statement (1) is correct.
questions.explanation_hi:
आधिकारिक उत्तर कुंजी (I.A.S. (Pre) 2010): विकल्प (A) सही है।
विस्तृत व्याख्या (Ghatnachakra Official Notes):
96.5% of the total water available on Earth is salt water found 
in Ocean. Out of the remaining 2.5% Fresh water, 1.7% is in 
the form of glaciers and polar ice, which is unusable for us. 
So in this way total available fresh water to use is less than 
1% of the total water available on earth. Out of total amount 
of fresh water (2.5%), 68.7% is found in the form of glaciers 
and polar ice, 30.1% in the form of underground water, 0.3% 
in the form of surface water and remaining 0.9% is found in 
other forms. Hence only statement (1) is correct.
